summary: A tappable button: filled, outlined or text style, with an optional leading icon, optionally full width. Labelled for accessibility from its label; enabled (true/false, or a 0/1 variable or expression read at run time) dims it, drops the click and marks it disabled. The 40 dp pill sits in a 48 dp tall touch target.

label.doc: Button text; also its accessibility label

style.doc: filled: a solid pill (primary action); outlined: a 1.5 dp ring (secondary); text: label only (tertiary)

color.doc: Fill (filled), or ring and label (outlined, text)

surface.doc: outlined (and, in mono, filled and disabled): the colour the button sits on, which fills the inside of the ring. Pass @colors.surface for a button inside a Card

enabled.doc: true/false: fixed when expanded. Or a runtime value, "@canSubmit" or an expression ("@a * @b"), exactly 0 or 1: the button follows it while it plays (0: dimmed, the click does nothing, announced as disabled; 1: normal)

fill.doc: true: the button spans the width it is given (fillMaxWidth), its label centred: a form or dialog button

onClick.doc: Any click action (valueFloatChange, valueFloatExpressionChange, hostNamedAction, ...). Omitted: the button is not clickable

icon.doc: A leading icon about 16 dp square, drawn in the label colour (onPrimary for filled). Without it the label is the only child

pitfalls: The outlined ring is two stacked backgrounds, not a border: `border` cannot take a theme colour (json2rc and the Java parser write the @colors id as a literal, transparent, colour). So the inside is painted with `surface`: set it to whatever the button sits on (@colors.surface in a Card), or the ring shows a background-coloured fill

The height is fixed: a 40 dp pill (control_height) with 4 dp (space_1) of transparent padding above and below, so the button is 48 dp tall and all of it is clickable; the clip and ripple stay on the pill. Leave no extra vertical space between stacked buttons or rows of buttons (the padding is 8 dp of the gap). The width wraps the label, so give a row of buttons room or they overflow; a label under about 16 dp (one or two letters) leaves the target under 48 dp wide
The label is one line with an ellipsis (maxLines 1): in a slot narrower than the label it ends in … instead of wrapping and being clipped by the pill

A runtime enabled ("@var" or an expression) writes the button twice, a disabled face and an enabled one, each shown by a visibility variable (enabled and 1 - enabled, computed from resources): only the enabled face has the click, ripple and onClick, so at 0 a tap runs nothing and sends no host action. It costs about 490 B more per call than a literal (plus the icon slot, written twice), so use a literal true/false when the state is fixed. The value must be exactly 0 or 1 and must read only resources variables (a host variable, an exported one), not a tree variable. A disabled face has no click to merge its text, so its label is on the text alone, marked disabled: one item for a screen reader, in both states. Its focus box is the text, not the pill
fill: true spans the width the parent gives (fillMaxWidth) with the label centred; in a row give it a weight instead or it takes the whole row
